notes.text: **Genesis 25:19** — וְאֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת יִצְחָק בֶּן אַבְרָהָם אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק. “These are the offspring of Isaac son of Abraham: Abraham begot Isaac.” The doubled “Abraham … Abraham” is the hook for the whole os, taken up at [1.31] and again at [4.1]. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Genesis 25:17; correct: Genesis 25:19)*

**Midrash Tanchuma, Toldot 2** — זֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב גִּיל יָגִיל אֲבִי צַדִּיק וְיוֹלֵד חָכָם יִשְׂמַח בּוֹ. כְּנֶגֶד מִי אֲמָרוֹ שְׁלֹמֹה? לֹא אֲמָרוֹ אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד יִצְחָק, שֶׁבְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד יִצְחָק, הָיוּ הַכֹּל שְׂמֵחִים … וְאֵין בְּרִיתִי אֶלָּא יִצְחָק, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְאֶת בְּרִיתִי אָקִים אֶת יִצְחָק. Solomon's verse was said about Isaac: at his birth all creation rejoiced, because without Isaac — God's “covenant” — the world would not endure.
Rav Tzadok's “etc.” passes over the Midrash's reason (the world's existence depends on Isaac) and its proof-verse, Genesis 17:21. *Mafteach: found*

**Proverbs 23:24** — גִּיל יָגִיל אֲבִי צַדִּיק וְיוֹלֵד חָכָם יִשְׂמַח בּוֹ. “The father of a righteous one will surely rejoice; one who begets a wise son will be glad in him.” Rav Tzadok reads the first half at [1.16] and the second half at [1.26] as being about Jacob, the son, so that the rejoicing “father” is Isaac. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Proverbs 63:25 (second half only); correct: Proverbs 23:24)*

**Jeremiah 33:25** — אִם לֹא בְרִיתִי יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה חֻקּוֹת שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ לֹא שָׂמְתִּי (as cited in Tanchuma, Toldot 2). “Were it not for My covenant by day and night, I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth.” At [1.10]–[1.12] Rav Tzadok maps each phrase of the verse onto one of the Midrash's rejoicing pairs. *Mafteach: wrong label (index: book given as Yechezkel; key Jeremiah 33:25 is right)*

**Yevamot 20a** — אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַיֵּים דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים, קָדוֹשׁ הוּא דְּלָא מִיקְּרֵי, רָשָׁע נָמֵי לָא מִיקְּרֵי! Rava objects: is someone who ignores the words of the Sages merely “not holy”? Is he not called wicked as well? Rav Tzadok takes the conclusion: breaking even a rabbinic rule makes one a *rasha*, so the plain title *tzaddik* is left for someone who never sinned. *Mafteach: found*

**Niddah 12a** — אָמַר רָבָא: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַיֵּים דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים — ״צָנוּעַ״ הוּא דְּלָא מִקְּרֵי, הָא ״רָשָׁע״ לָא מִקְּרֵי? Rava makes the same objection in another context: one who does not keep the Sages' words is surely called wicked, not merely “not modest.” *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Niddah, no daf; correct: Niddah 12a)*

**Bava Metzia 84a** (unnamed background) — שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ מֵעֵין שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן. “The beauty of Jacob our father was like the beauty of Adam.” The Talmud's comparison of Jacob to Adam stands behind Rav Tzadok's claim that Jacob was “like Adam before the fall.” *Mafteach: missing*

**Genesis 21:4** — וַיָּמָל אַבְרָהָם אֶת יִצְחָק בְּנוֹ בֶּן שְׁמֹנַת יָמִים כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים. “Abraham circumcised his son Isaac at eight days, as God had commanded him.” Isaac was the first to be circumcised on the eighth day, holy from birth, and that is what makes him able to father Jacob. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Machshavot Charutz 19:4** (Rav Tzadok) — Adam was created circumcised and became uncircumcised through the sin. Abraham was the first to be circumcised in order to repair this, “וְהוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹלָדָה כֵן”. This supplies the link to Adam before the sin that the os assumes at [1.19]. *checked*

**Yoma 28b** — אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, זָקֵן וְיוֹשֵׁב בִּישִׁיבָה; and further on: קִיֵּים אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַע אַבְרָהָם בְּקוֹלִי״. Abraham was an elder who headed an academy, and he kept the entire Torah before it was given. These are the two claims Rav Tzadok makes: Abraham taught Torah, and Abraham kept all of it. *Mafteach: found*

**Micah 7:20** — תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתָּ לַאֲבֹתֵינוּ מִימֵי קֶדֶם. “Grant truth to Jacob, kindness to Abraham.” Truth, which is Torah, belongs to Jacob, and this makes him the unqualified *chacham*. *Mafteach: found*
**Berakhot 5b** — ״אֱמֶת״ — זוֹ תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֱמֶת קְנֵה וְאַל תִּמְכֹּר״. “‘Truth’ means Torah, as it says: ‘Buy truth and do not sell it.’” *Mafteach: found*

**Sanhedrin 97a; Avodah Zarah 9a** — תָּנָא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ: שֵׁשֶׁת אֲלָפִים שָׁנָה הָוֵי עָלְמָא, שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹהוּ, שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה, שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ. The world's six millennia are two of chaos, two of Torah and two of Mashiach. In Avodah Zarah 9a the Gemara dates the start of the Torah era to Abraham, which is the point Rav Tzadok needs. *Mafteach: found*

**Midrash Tanchuma, Toldot 4** — אַבְרָהָם נִתְעַטֵּר בִּזְכוּת יַעֲקֹב. כְּשֶׁהִשְׁלִיךְ אוֹתוֹ נִמְרוֹד לְתוֹךְ הַכִּבְשָׁן … אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, לָזֶה אַתָּה מַצִּיל? כַּמָּה רְשָׁעִים עֲתִידִין לַעֲמֹד מִמֶּנּוּ … בִּשְׁבִיל יַעֲקֹב בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁעָתִיד לַעֲמֹד מִמֶּנּוּ, אֲנִי מַצִּילוֹ. When Nimrod threw Abraham into the furnace, the angels objected to his rescue because of the wicked who would descend from him. God answered that He was saving him for the sake of Jacob.
The same section goes on to the passages Rav Tzadok takes up in paragraphs 3 and 4: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁנִּתְעַטְּרוּ בָנִים בִּשְׁבִיל אָבוֹת … אֲבָל יִצְחָק נִתְעַטֵּר בְּאַבְרָהָם, וְאַבְרָהָם נִתְעַטֵּר בְּיִצְחָק. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Tanchuma, no section; correct: Midrash Tanchuma, Toldot 4)*

**Proverbs 17:6** — עֲטֶרֶת זְקֵנִים בְּנֵי בָנִים וְתִפְאֶרֶת בָּנִים אֲבוֹתָם. “Grandchildren are the crown of elders, and the glory of children is their fathers.” The Midrash reads the first half as fathers crowned by their descendants (paragraph 2) and the second half as children crowned by their fathers (paragraph 3). *Mafteach: found*

**Rosh Hashanah 16b** — וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: אֵין דָּנִין אֶת הָאָדָם אֶלָּא לְפִי מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי שָׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶל קוֹל הַנַּעַר בַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא שָׁם״. A person is judged only by his deeds at that moment, as with Ishmael. Rav Tzadok argues that if a person's own future sins are not held against him, his descendants' sins certainly should not be. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Shem MiShmuel, Toldot 4 (5673)** (Chassidus) — The passage begins with Tanchuma's joy at Isaac's birth and then raises the same objection Rav Tzadok raises here. Using the same Rosh Hashanah 16b, it asks how the angels could hold future wicked descendants against Abraham. Its answer differs from Rav Tzadok's: the angels were not accusing him but proposing that it would be better for him not to father dross, until God showed that Jacob would come out pure.
וְזֶה תֵּימָא שֶׁלֹּא מָצִינוּ קִטְרוּג שֶׁיִּתְחַיֵּב הַצַּדִּיק בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁעָתִיד לְהוֹלִיד רְשָׁעִים

**Yefeh To'ar** (R. Shmuel Yafeh Ashkenazi's commentary on Midrash Rabbah) — Rav Tzadok cites its view that one who gives his life to sanctify the Name is miraculously saved only when others need him, as with Rabbi Akiva, who was not saved. The Yefeh To'ar is not in any text collection available here (searched the Akiva source and genre corpora and Sefaria), so its wording is not quoted. *Mafteach: missing*

**Menachot 29b** — אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְזוֹ שְׂכָרָהּ? אָמַר לוֹ: שְׁתוֹק, כָּךְ עָלָה בְּמַחְשָׁבָה לְפָנַי. Shown Rabbi Akiva's martyrdom, Moses asked, “This is Torah, and this its reward?” and was told, “Be silent; so it arose in thought before Me.” Rav Tzadok reads “thought” first as Rabbi Akiva's own desire ([2.15]) and then as God's primordial thought, which leads to light out of darkness ([2.19]–[2.21]). *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Menachot, no daf; correct: Menachot 29b)*

**Berakhot 61b** — אָמַר לָהֶם: כׇּל יָמַי הָיִיתִי מִצְטַעֵר עַל פָּסוּק זֶה ״בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ״ — אֲפִילּוּ נוֹטֵל אֶת נִשְׁמָתְךָ. “All my days I was troubled by this verse, ‘with all your soul,’ even if He takes your soul…” This shows that Rabbi Akiva had long wanted martyrdom, a desire Rav Tzadok does not find recorded of Abraham. *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 1:2–3** — וְהָאָרֶץ הָיְתָה תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ וְחֹשֶׁךְ עַל פְּנֵי תְהוֹם … וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יְהִי אוֹר וַיְהִי אוֹר. In Creation itself darkness and void come first and “Let there be light” follows. Rav Tzadok reads this as the meaning of “so it arose in thought before Me.” *Mafteach: missing*

**Zohar II 184a** (Tetzaveh) — דְּלֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא, דְּכַד אִתְכַּפְיָא סִטְרָא דָּא, אִסְתַּלָּק קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְעֵילָּא … וְלֵית טוּבָא אֶלָּא מִגּוֹ בִּישָׁא. “There is no light except what comes out of darkness … and no good except from within evil.” Rabbi Akiva's level had to come out of his early darkness and his ordeal. *Mafteach: found*
**Job 28:10** — בַּצּוּרוֹת יְאֹרִים בִּקֵּעַ וְכָל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ. “He cuts channels in the rocks, and his eye sees every precious thing.” *Mafteach: found*

**Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6; Midrash Tanchuma, Chukat 8** — דְּבָרִים שֶׁלֹּא נִגְלוּ לְמֹשֶׁה נִגְלוּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וַחֲבֵרָיו. וְכָל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ, זֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וַחֲבֵרָיו. “Things not revealed to Moses were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues.” Rav Tzadok identifies this added knowledge with the Fiftieth Gate ([2.25]). *Mafteach: found*

**Rosh Hashanah 21b** — חֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה נִבְרְאוּ בָּעוֹלָם, וְכוּלָּן נִיתְּנוּ לְמֹשֶׁה, חָסֵר אֶחָד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַתְּחַסְּרֵהוּ מְעַט מֵאֱלֹהִים״. Fifty gates of understanding were created, and Moses received all but one. Rav Tzadok's point is that the fiftieth gate belongs to the *ba'al teshuvah*, and that is why it was missing for Moses. *Mafteach: found*

**Exodus 2:2; Megillah 14a** — וַתֵּרֶא אֹתוֹ כִּי טוֹב הוּא; and the Gemara: וּבְשָׁעָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד נִתְמַלֵּא כָּל הַבַּיִת כּוּלּוֹ אוֹרָה. Moses was “good” from birth, and the house filled with light when he was born. Because his starting point was light, the gate that is reached only from darkness stayed closed to him. *Mafteach: missing*

**Pesachim 49b** — תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי עַם הָאָרֶץ אָמַרְתִּי מִי יִתֵּן לִי תַּלְמִיד חָכָם וְאֶנְשְׁכֶנּוּ כַּחֲמוֹר. “When I was an ignoramus I said: if only I had a Torah scholar, I would bite him like a donkey.” Rabbi Akiva began in the dark, as an ignoramus who hated scholars, and so he is the model penitent who reaches the Fiftieth Gate. *Mafteach: found*

**Bereshit Rabbah 8:5** — בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבְרֹאת אֶת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, נַעֲשׂוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת כִּתִּים כִּתִּים … מֵהֶם אוֹמְרִים אַל יִבָּרֵא … וֶאֱמֶת אוֹמֵר אַל יִבָּרֵא, שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שְׁקָרִים. When man was about to be created, some of the ministering angels said he should not be, because he would be full of falsehood. Rav Tzadok identifies these as the same angels who objected to saving Abraham: their concern is the mixture of good and evil, not accusation. *Mafteach: missing*

**Genesis 5:24 with Rashi** — וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ חֲנוֹךְ אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים וְאֵינֶנּוּ כִּי לָקַח אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים; Rashi: צַדִּיק הָיָה וְקַל בְּדַעְתּוֹ לָשׁוּב לְהַרְשִׁיעַ, לְפִיכָךְ מִהֵר הַקָּבָּ״ה וְסִלְּקוֹ. Enoch was righteous but likely to turn wicked, so God removed him early. Rav Tzadok has the angels propose the same for Abraham. *Mafteach: missing*

**Mishnah Sanhedrin 10:1 (Sanhedrin 90a)** — כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים. “All Israel have a share in the World to Come.” For Rav Tzadok this shows that from Jacob on, good and evil are no longer mixed in the nation. *Mafteach: found*

**Isaiah 60:21** — וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ נֵצֶר מַטָּעַי מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַי לְהִתְפָּאֵר. “Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.” *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 31:42** — לוּלֵי אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם וּפַחַד יִצְחָק הָיָה לִי כִּי עַתָּה רֵיקָם שִׁלַּחְתָּנִי. “Had not the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, been with me, you would have sent me away empty-handed.” Tanchuma (Toldot 4) concludes: הֱוֵי, זְכוּת אַבְרָהָם הִצִּילַתּוּ לְיַעֲקֹב. Rav Tzadok asks why the Midrash names only Abraham when the verse mentions Isaac too. *Mafteach: found*

**Berakhot 58a** — בְּמַתְנִיתָא תַּנָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: ״לְךָ ה׳ הַגְּדֻלָּה״ — זוֹ קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף, ״וְהַגְּבוּרָה״ — זוֹ מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת, ״וְהַתִּפְאֶרֶת״ — זוֹ מַתַּן תּוֹרָה. In Rabbi Akiva's reading of I Chronicles 29:11, “the glory” is the Giving of the Torah. This lets Rav Tzadok read “the glory of children is their fathers” as: the Torah that Israel received came through the merit of the Patriarchs. *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 15:14** — וְגַם אֶת הַגּוֹי אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹדוּ דָּן אָנֹכִי וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל. “Afterward they will go out with great wealth.” Rav Tzadok reads the “great wealth” promised to Abraham as, above all, the Torah received after the Exodus. *Mafteach: missing*

**Exodus 3:12** — וְזֶה לְּךָ הָאוֹת כִּי אָנֹכִי שְׁלַחְתִּיךָ בְּהוֹצִיאֲךָ אֶת הָעָם מִמִּצְרַיִם תַּעַבְדוּן אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים עַל הָהָר הַזֶּה. The purpose of the Exodus is service at Sinai. *Mafteach: found*

**Exodus 20:2–3** — אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִיךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים. לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים עַל פָּנָי. These first two commandments are the roots that Rav Tzadok assigns to Abraham (positive commandments) and Isaac (negative commandments). *Mafteach: missing*

**Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2:4** — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל: אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ, נִתְקַע תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה בְּלִבָּם … רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אָמַר בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל: לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ, נֶעֱקַר מִלִּבָּם יֵצֶר הָרָע. At “I am,” Torah was fixed in their hearts. At “You shall not have,” the evil inclination was uprooted.
Etz Yosef there (1:2:4:1) already makes the equation Rav Tzadok states at [3.13]: וְאָנֹכִי כּוֹלֵל כָּל מִצְוֹת עֲשֵׂה, וְלֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ כּוֹלֵל מִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה. *Mafteach: found*
**Chullin 16a** — וְהָא קְרָא קָאָמַר! קְרָא זְרִיזוּתֵיהּ דְּאַבְרָהָם קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן. The verse “Abraham rose early” teaches Abraham's alacrity, not a law of slaughter. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 7:2–3** (Rav Tzadok) — It makes the same division: positive commandments come from love, Abraham's trait, and guarding the negative commandments comes from fear, Isaac's trait. It cites the same Chullin 16a and Rashi on the Rif, and adds the Yerushalmi “עֲשֵׂה מֵאַהֲבָה … שֶׁאִם בָּאתָ לִבְעֹט דַּע שֶׁאַתָּה יָרֵא” together with Yoma 28b on alacrity. *checked*

notes.anchor: רַשִׁ״י לָרִי״ף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
notes.text: **Rashi on the Rif, Avodah Zarah ch. 1** — Rav Tzadok cites it for the rule that *zerizut* (alacrity) applies to positive commandments and *zehirut* (caution) to negative ones. He cites it again for this in Chayei Sara 7:3. Rashi's commentary on the Rif is not in any text collection available here, so the wording is not quoted. *Mafteach: missing*

**Ecclesiastes 10:2** — לֵב חָכָם לִימִינוֹ וְלֵב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ. “The wise man's heart is at his right, the fool's heart at his left.” The “left” heart is where the evil inclination is, and Isaac's fear is what roots it out. *Mafteach: missing*

**Psalms 34:15** — סוּר מֵרָע וַעֲשֵׂה טוֹב בַּקֵּשׁ שָׁלוֹם וְרָדְפֵהוּ. In Rav Tzadok's scheme, “turn from evil” comes before “do good”: Isaac's refining fear has to come first so that Abraham's Torah can take hold. *Mafteach: missing*

**Genesis 24:1** — וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים וַה' בֵּרַךְ אֶת אַבְרָהָם בַּכֹּל. The verse comes right after the Akeidah. Rav Tzadok reads Abraham's being “old” as completion up to the highest root. *Mafteach: found*

**Zohar I, Chayei Sara** (Sefaria, Zohar Chayei Sara 16:120) — וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן, וּכְדֵין בָּא בַּיָּמִים בְּאִינוּן יוֹמִין עִלָּאִין בְּאִינוּן יוֹמִין יְדִיעָאן בְּרָזָא דִמְהֵימְנוּתָא. “Advanced in days” refers to the supernal days, the *sefirot*. The same reading also appears at Zohar III, Sh'lach (Sefaria 33:246). *Mafteach: missing*

**Bava Metzia 87a** — עַד אַבְרָהָם לֹא הָיָה זִקְנָה … אֲתָא אַבְרָהָם בְּעָא רַחֲמֵי וַהֲוָה זִקְנָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים״. “Until Abraham there was no old age.” In the Gemara this is about outward signs of age. Rav Tzadok reads it as the first attainment of “age” in the sense of the *Atika* level. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Noach 9:3** (Rav Tzadok) — It sets out the scheme assumed here: the ten trials ascend through the ten *sefirot*. The ninth trial corresponds to *Chokhmah*, and the Akeidah corresponds to *Keter*, “נֶעְלַם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן”. In it God refined Abraham to the root, וְזָכָה לִבְחִי' זָקֵן … בְּיוֹמִין עִלָּאִין. Noach 9 adds that the first nine trials were Abraham's own effort, while the Akeidah was the refinement from God's side. *checked*

notes.anchor: כִּי עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה
notes.text: **Genesis 22:12** — אַל תִּשְׁלַח יָדְךָ אֶל הַנַּעַר … כִּי עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה וְלֹא חָשַׂכְתָּ אֶת בִּנְךָ אֶת יְחִידְךָ מִמֶּנִּי. At the climax of the Akeidah Abraham is praised for fear, not love. This is the key text for “Abraham was crowned through Isaac” ([4.29]–[4.31]). *Mafteach: found*
**Isaiah 41:8** — וְאַתָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל עַבְדִּי יַעֲקֹב אֲשֶׁר בְּחַרְתִּיךָ זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי. “The seed of Abraham who loved Me.” *Mafteach: missing*

**Peri Tzadik, Noach 9:2** (his own sefer) — שעפ"י דִּין תּוֹרָה לֹא הָיָה נִצְרָךְ אאע"ה לִמְסֹור א"ע לְהַשְׁלִיכוֹ לַכִּבְשָׁן שב"נ אֵינוֹ מְצֻוֶּוה עַל קְדֻושָּׁה הַשֵּׁם. Strictly by law Abraham did not have to let himself be thrown into the furnace: a Noahide is not commanded to sanctify the Name (Sanhedrin 74b), and on the Rambam's view he would even be liable for his own life. He gave himself up only to make God's kingship known. *Mafteach: missing*

**Sanhedrin 89b** — כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַפַּרְגּוֹד: הַשֶּׂה לְעוֹלָה וְאֵין יִצְחָק לְעוֹלָה. אָמַר לוֹ: כָּךְ עׇנְשׁוֹ שֶׁל בַּדַּאי, שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אָמַר אֱמֶת אֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ. Satan said he had heard that the lamb, not Isaac, would be the offering. Abraham answered that a liar is not believed even when he tells the truth. Rav Tzadok takes this as a sign that Abraham himself sensed that Isaac would not be the offering. *Mafteach: found*

**Bereshit Rabbah 56:4** — אָמַר לוֹ לְמָחָר אוֹמֵר לְךָ שׁוֹפֵךְ דָּם אַתְּ חַיָּב שֶׁשָּׁפַכְתָּ דָּמוֹ שֶׁל בִּנְךָ, אָמַר לוֹ, עַל מְנָת כֵּן. Samael warned that tomorrow God would call him a murderer for shedding his son's blood, and Abraham answered, “Even so.” Abraham did not deny that he might be acting wrongly; he obeyed out of fear anyway. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Bereshit Rabbah 56:7; correct: Bereshit Rabbah 56:4)*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 5:2** (Rav Tzadok) — It cites this os by name (“נִתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל מַאֲמָר א”) and adds an identification: Abraham crowned with Isaac's fear is the crown of *nishma* (guarding the negative commandments, “עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַעְתָּ בְּקֹלִי”), and Isaac crowned with Abraham's love is the crown of *na'aseh*. On this basis it explains the names Yishmael and Esav and Isaac's love for Esav. *checked*
**Peri Tzadik, Parshat Shekalim 7** (Rav Tzadok) — It retells the Akeidah argument of [4.15]–[4.22] almost word for word and refers back here (“ונת' תולדות מא' א' ד"ה ומסיק”). It adds that this completed Abraham “in ten times ten” and links the result to the 400 shekels for the Cave of Machpelah and to Moses' crowns. *checked*
**Peri Tzadik, Pesach 52:1** (Rav Tzadok) — It sets out the same pair of ideas: the perfection of love comes through fear at the Akeidah, and the perfection of fear comes from love. It cites the same Zohar (אִתְכְּלִיל אֶשָּׁא בְּמַיָּא) and the same line from Tanna DeBei Eliyahu, and adds that fear is likened to gold. *checked*

**R. Menachem Azaryah of Fano (Rama MiPano), Asarah Ma'amarot** — “נֶפֶשׁ הָאָב מַזָּל לַבֵּן.” Rav Tzadok quotes this often and names the book (Peri Tzadik, Kedoshim 7:1: “ובס' עשרה מאמרות דנפשות האבות מזל לבנים”; Nasso 2:3). The father's soul is the son's *mazal*, the root above him that surrounds him. Asarah Ma'amarot is not in any text collection available here, so its own wording is not quoted. *Mafteach: missing*

**Megillah 3a** — וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּלָא חֲזוֹ, מַאי טַעְמָא אִיבְּעִיתוּ? אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא חֲזוֹ, מַזָּלַיְיהוּ חֲזוֹ. Daniel's companions were terrified even though they did not see the vision, because their *mazal* saw it. *Mazal* perceives what the person's own awareness does not reach. *Mafteach: found*

**Zohar III 79b** (Acharei Mot; Sefaria 74:3, 75:1) — on the word *al* in “וַתִּתְפַּלֵּל עַל ה'” (I Samuel 1:10): עַל דַּיְיקָא, בְּגִין דִּבְנִין בְּמַזָּלָא קַדִּישָׁא תַּלְיָין; and on “הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל ה' יְהָבְךָ” (Psalms 55:23): עַל דַּיְיקָא, דְּהָא מְזוֹנֵי בְּמַזָּלָא תַּלְיָין. Children and sustenance hang on the holy *mazala*, so the verse says “*al* Hashem”. This is the verse-reading Rav Tzadok means by “על הפסוק”. Checked on III 79b through Sefaria's page division. *Mafteach: found*

**Moed Katan 28a** (the underlying dictum) — אָמַר רָבָא: חַיֵּי בְּנֵי וּמְזוֹנֵי לָא בִּזְכוּתָא תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא אֶלָּא בְּמַזָּלָא תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא. Life, children and livelihood depend not on merit but on *mazal*. *Mafteach: wrong label (index: book given as Chagigah; key Moed Katan 28a is right)*

**Vayikra Rabbah 36:5; Rashi on Genesis 47:31** — עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהָיְתָה מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה לְפָנָיו, אַבְרָהָם יָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ יִשְׁמָעֵאל … יִצְחָק יָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ עֵשָׂו … אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה, כָּל בָּנָיו צַדִּיקִים. Jacob's “bed was complete”: unlike Abraham and Isaac, all his children were righteous. *Mafteach: missing*
**Genesis 27:19** — וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב אֶל אָבִיו אָנֹכִי עֵשָׂו בְּכֹרֶךָ. “I am Esau your firstborn.” Toldot 5–6 return to this verse. *Mafteach: found*

**Zohar I 143a** (Toldot) — יְיָ הַצִּילָה נַפְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת שֶׁקֶר מִלָּשׁוֹן רְמִיָה, דָּא הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְעֵשָׂו שַׁרְיָא בֵּיהּ, דְּאִיהוּ שְׂפַת שֶׁקֶר. Jacob prayed to be saved from the “lying lip,” which the Zohar identifies as the level that rests on Esau. That is, he prayed to be saved from Esau's falsehood, not from a lie of his own. *Mafteach: found*
**Psalms 120:2** — ה' הַצִּילָה נַפְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת שֶׁקֶר מִלָּשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה. “Lord, save my soul from lying lips, from a deceitful tongue.” *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 25:28** — וַיֶּאֱהַב יִצְחָק אֶת עֵשָׂו כִּי צַיִד בְּפִיו. “Isaac loved Esau because game was in his mouth.” Rav Tzadok cites the Arizal (no place given) for reading the “game” as Rabbi Meir's soul, hidden in Esau's line. In the Arizal's writings the verse is read as holy sparks of Isaac's own soul held in Esau: **Sha'ar Ma'amarei Razal, Midrashim 2**: וְזֶהוּ טַעַם וַיֶּאֱהַב יִצְחָק אֶת עֵשָׂו כִּי צַיִד בְּפִיו, לִהְיוֹת כִּי הָיָה לוֹ צַד נִיצוֹצֵי הַקְּדוֹשָׁה מֵחֵלֶק הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁל יִצְחָק ... וְהָיוּ בְּרֵישֵׁיהּ דְּעֵשָׂו, which is why Esau's head was buried with Isaac (also **Pri Etz Chaim, Sha'ar Rosh Chodesh, Chanukah and Purim 3**). That Rabbi Meir, descended from Nero (Gittin 56a), is that spark is not stated there; **Kav HaYashar 102** connects Rabbi Meir from Nero with repairing Esau's flaw. Rav Tzadok gives the full reading in Chanukah 11 and Kedushat Shabbat 6. *Mafteach: missing*
**Gittin 56a** — עֲרַק וַאֲזַל וְאִיגַּיַּיר, וּנְפַק מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר. Nero fled, converted, and Rabbi Meir descended from him. *Mafteach: found*
**Sanhedrin 86a** — דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: סְתָם מַתְנִיתִין – רַבִּי מֵאִיר. An unattributed Mishnah follows Rabbi Meir, so Rabbi Meir is the root of the Oral Torah. *Mafteach: missing*

**Zohar I 133b** (Chayei Sara) — וּבְקַדְמִיתָא אִתְכְּלִיל כְּחֲדָא אֶשָׁא בְּמַיָא. אֵימָתַי, בְּשַׁעְתָּא דְּעָקַד לֵיהּ לְיִצְחָק לְמֶעְבַּד בֵּיהּ דִּינָא כְּדֵין אִתְכְּלִיל אֶשָׁא בְּמַיָא. וְהַשְׁתָּא אִתְכְּלִילוּ מַיָא בְּאֶשָׁא. At the Akeidah fire (Isaac) was included in water (Abraham); now water is included in fire. The same idea, tied to “וְהָאֱלֹהִים נִסָּה אֶת אַבְרָהָם,” is at Zohar I 119b. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 73:1** (Ishbitz–Radzin) — It quotes Zohar I 119b: Abraham, who had no judgment in him, had to be included in judgment. Isaac too כַּד אִתְעֲקַד … אִתְעַטַּר בְּאַתְרֵיהּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ דְּאַבְרָהָם וְאִתְכְּלִיל אֶשָּׁא בְּמַיָּא. This is the Zohar's own wording for the crowning in both directions. Sod Yesharim adds that the trial showed Abraham had no will in his heart other than God's own will, which wanted Isaac to live. *checked*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Shem MiShmuel, Rosh Hashanah 17:4** (Chassidus) — It treats the Akeidah as the trial against Abraham's nature of kindness, in which, according to the Zohar, water and fire were included in each other. It explains this as Abraham's whole self being set aside before God's will in sanctifying the Name.
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁכָּךְ עִנְיַן הִתְכַּלְּלוּת מַיָּא בְּאֶשָּׁא וְאֶשָּׁא בְּמַיָּא, שֶׁלַּעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִתְבַּטְּלָה מְצִיאוּתוֹ

**Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 3:1** — עוֹד אָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ … אֲנִי יָרֵאתִי מִתּוֹךְ שִׂמְחָתִי וְשָׂמַחְתִּי מִתּוֹךְ יִרְאָתִי, וְאַהֲבָתִי עָלְתָה עַל כֻּלָּם. David: “I feared from within my joy and rejoiced from within my fear, and my love rose above them all.” *Mafteach: wrong label (index: Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 3)*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Sefat Emet, Devarim, Vaetchanan 16:5** (Chassidus) — It uses the same Tanna DeBei Eliyahu line in the same way: love and fear complete each other, and the love of Shabbat is meant to add fear during the weekdays.
וְכֵן עַל יְדֵי אַהֲבָה שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת יֵשׁ לְהוֹסִיף הַיִּרְאָה בִּימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה כְּעִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ יָרֵאתִי מִתּוֹךְ שִׂמְחָתִי וְשָׂמַחְתִּי מִתּוֹךְ יִרְאָתִי

**Shabbat 88a** — בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נַעֲשֶׂה לְנִשְׁמָע בָּאוּ שִׁשִּׁים רִיבּוֹא שֶׁל מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת, לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל קָשְׁרוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי כְתָרִים, אֶחָד כְּנֶגֶד נַעֲשֶׂה וְאֶחָד כְּנֶגֶד נִשְׁמָע. Rav Tzadok links the two crowns to “I am” and “You shall not have,” that is, to Abraham's love and Isaac's fear. *Mafteach: found*

**Bereshit Rabbah 63:2** — עֲטֶרֶת זְקֵנִים בְּנֵי בָנִים … אַבְרָהָם לֹא נִצֹּל מִכִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ אֶלָּא בִּזְכוּת שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב, מָשָׁל לְאֶחָד … שֶׁהוּא עָתִיד לְהוֹלִיד בַּת וְהִיא נִשַּׂאת לַמֶּלֶךְ, אָמַר כְּדַאי הוּא לְהִנָּצֵל בִּזְכוּת בִּתּוֹ. The condemned man is spared because the daughter he will father is to marry the king. *Mafteach: missing*

**Song of Songs 3:11** — צְאֶינָה וּרְאֶינָה בְּנוֹת צִיּוֹן בַּמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה בָּעֲטָרָה שֶׁעִטְּרָה לּוֹ אִמּוֹ בְּיוֹם חֲתֻנָּתוֹ וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַת לִבּוֹ. The verse speaks of a crown and a wedding day, so it ties the Midrash's parable of the daughter who marries the king to the Torah's crowns. *Mafteach: found*

**Mishnah Taanit 4:8 (Taanit 26b)** — ״בְּיוֹם חֲתֻנָּתוֹ״ — זֶה מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, ״וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַת לִבּוֹ״ — זֶה בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ. “The day of his wedding” is the Giving of the Torah. *Mafteach: found*

**Shabbat 88a** — וְכֵיוָן שֶׁחָטְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל יָרְדוּ מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים רִיבּוֹא מַלְאֲכֵי חַבָּלָה וּפֵירְקוּם … אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְכוּלָּן זָכָה מֹשֶׁה וּנְטָלָן … אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲזִירָן לָנוּ. After the Golden Calf the crowns were taken away and Moses received them all; in the future God will give them back. *Mafteach: found*

**Pri Etz Chaim, Sha'ar HaShabbat 8** (R. Chaim Vital, from the Arizal), on *Yismach Moshe* — אַמְנָם בְּכָל עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּלַּיְלָה חוֹזֵר מֹשֶׁה וּמְקַבֵּל הָאֶלֶף חֲלָקִים שֶׁאָבַד ... וְאָז מַחֲזִיר הַכְּתָרִים שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לָהֶם. Every Shabbat eve Moses receives back the thousand portions of light he lost through Israel's sin, and then he returns to Israel their crowns, from which they inherit the added holiness of Shabbat. The Arizal reads *Yismach Moshe* this way: Moses rejoices in his own restored portion and gives back the crowns he held in trust. *Mafteach: missing (now added)*
